subject: Data retention exception request — post-call recaps & next steps

Subject: Post-call: Data handling & retention requirements (FinSecure)

Thanks again for taking time this morning, Olivia — good conversation. Quick recap of the requirements we captured and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned:

Summary of FinSecure requirements (from today's discovery):
- PII handling: no persistent storage of any user-submitted PII or sensitive fields (SSNs, account numbers, raw PII) — preference for 0-retention for request/response bodies.
- Troubleshooting logs: FinSecure is open to very short retention for operational telemetry (if needed) — target 7 days or less.
- Data residency: US-only (US-East preferred).
- Encryption & keys: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for at-rest encryption.
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 report and configuration screenshots for logging controls.

Open questions where we said we'd follow up:
1) Is 0-retention for request/response bodies achievable on Hosted (no-persist) or will Private/Dedicated be required for guarantee?
2) Can we produce a technical runbook describing how we redact or avoid logging PII end-to-end?
3) Procurement/legal: next steps for a DPA + retention exception sign-off and timeline for procurement.

Proposed next steps:
- Rafael will follow up with technical options and limitations (we flagged KV cache, debugging traces).
- We'll prepare a short retention matrix showing options (Hosted w/ no-persist, Dedicated + config, Private deployment). Attached the initial retention_matrix.xlsx for your review.
- Marissa will follow up with commercial options and timelines.
- If OK, we'd like to schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your security team next week.

Attachments: retention_matrix.xlsx

Thanks — Camila

Subject: RE: Post-call: Data handling & retention requirements (FinSecure)

Thanks, Camila — quick technical note from the runtime side based on today's call. High-level options and tradeoffs: 

1) Hosted API (fastest):
- We support a "no-persist" flag that prevents storing request/response bodies in long-term logs. However, ephemeral traces and short-lived debugging traces may still be written to secure internal stores for max 24-72 hours depending on the incident window.
- Default KV cache and batching do not persist user PII across sessions, but there are runtime caches (KV cache for model context) which we can configure to evict immediately.
- We can offer a hosted configuration that redacts fields specified by FinSecure before persistence; redaction is client-side or via a pre-processing hook.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Gives you per-tenant isolation and tighter controls on retention policies. We can reduce operational telemetry to 7 days and configure node-level logs to exclude request/response payloads.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem):
- Full control: customer-managed networking and storage. With Private, we can ensure zero retention of request/response bodies by disabling persistence entirely and configuring KMS integration for keys you own. This is the only way to get a cryptographic guarantee that nothing leaves your environment.

Recommended approach (technical):
- If FinSecure requires a formal 0-retention guarantee for any PII, recommend Private deployment.
- If business prefers Hosted, we can propose a hosted 'no-persist' offering plus a contractually-scoped retention exception (security review required).

I've attached a short technical-options-summary.pdf that maps each option to the controls and residual risks. Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the time yesterday — quick commercial / timeline note to help procurement planning.

Options and high-level pricing implications (ballpark):
- Hosted (no-persist): fastest to onboard, standard per-token pricing. Additional line item for the retention exception review and implementation support — estimated $10k one-time security review + config and 1 week to implement after approval.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commit (starting ~$40k/month depending on throughput) — allows tighter retention controls and isolated telemetry.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): enterprise licensing, multi-week onboarding, includes KMS integrations and guaranteed no external persistence — recommended if you need legal guarantees on 0-retention.

Procurement path:
1) Please confirm preferred option (Hosted w/ no-persist + exception review vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) We'll open a security exception request (Sx-Req) and loop in Soojin for the review; target SLA for that review is 10 business days once the request is in.
3) Legal: we'll provide a DPA + proposed redlines. We can also accept a customer-supplied DPA.

I've attached a commercial-summary.pdf for the three paths. Also linking the HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/FS-2026-042.

If you confirm the Hosted path, we'll initiate the exception Sx-Req today and Rafael + Soojin will own the technical/security review.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@finsecure.co>

Date: 2026-03-22T14:50:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Data handling & retention requirements (FinSecure)

Thanks for the clear options. FinSecure's procurement and security teams discussed and here is our position: 

- We need 0-retention for any PII or raw user-submitted identifiers (no persistent storage of request/response bodies containing PII). If Redwood can guarantee this for Hosted, we will consider Hosted; otherwise we will evaluate Dedicated/Private.
- For operational telemetry (logs/metrics), we are willing to accept a maximum 7-day retention window, provided logs do not contain request/response payloads or identifiable PII.
- Data residency must be US (US-East).
- We require SOC 2 Type II evidence prior to signing and we need to use our KMS for encryption keys for at-rest storage if we choose Private.

Next steps for us:
- Please send the SOC 2 (redacted as necessary) and a technical runbook that shows exactly how PII is redacted/no-persist is implemented.
- We will circulate a DPA to your legal for review.
- Procurement timeline: we are targeting a signed agreement in 3–4 weeks, assuming the security review aligns.

Attached is our requirements doc for reference. Please confirm who at Redwood will own the Sx-Req and timeline.

Regards,
Olivia Chen
Head of Security Programs, FinSecure, Inc.
procurement@finsecure.co
